title: Spillover handling retro + weekly sync
content:
Purpose: quick retro + weekly sync focused on recent production spillover incidents, related kernel fallback behavior, and short-term mitigations for KV-prefetch/backpressure.

Attendees: Claire Huang (owner), Diego Ramirez (kernel), Aisha Khan (infra), Benji Morales (bench/obs), Ellen Park (oncall rotation), plus notes from oncall log (Anil).

High-level summary:
- This week we saw 3 discrete spillover incidents across two dedicated pods (eu-west-1) when median request lengths spiked at 1.8x baseline and batching heuristics triggered larger micro-batches.
- Root cause (hypothesis): a timing interaction between the adaptive batcher and the new prefetch window. Under bursty short-lived tails, the kernel transitioned to the fallback execution path which disables KV cache coalescing briefly; that caused higher CPU on the host and increased request queuing which in turn triggered spillover routing to lower-tier pools.
- Impact: increased p95 latency (~120ms -> ~280ms) for affected routes, ~6% request reroutes to fallback model variants, and one customer-facing error spike (auto-retries masked some errors).

Telemetry snapshot (Benji):
- Snapshot window: 2026-10-21 -> 2026-10-27
- Median seq len: 176 -> 316 on spike windows
- Prefetch hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 61% during incidents
- Batch size distribution shifted: 90th pct batch size from 4 -> 11
- Kernel fallback invocations: +420% in the two-hour window of the first incident

Actions taken during incident:
- Immediate: bump per-pod batching cap to 12 and enable temporary throttling policy to avoid cascading prefetch eviction (Aisha).
- Rollback: reverted experimental kernel patch that introduced aggressive small-kernel inlining (Diego).
- Observability: turned on verbose kernel traces for one pod for 48h (Benji).

Decisions and short-term mitigation (agreed in meeting):
1) Rework the batcher backoff logic so that when prefetch-hit drops below 70% we prefer smaller micro-batches rather than full fallback switch. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-11-09.
2) Add an intermediate kernel path that preserves KV coalescing when switching to the low-latency code path — prototype flag-only change to gate behavior. Owner: Diego + Claire. ETA: 2026-11-05 for flag; 2026-11-19 for end-to-end test.
3) Autoscaler smoothing: increase scale-down hysteresis from 60s -> 180s for dedicated pools with high prefetch variance. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2026-11-03.
4) Add a metric alert: prefetch-hit-rate < 65% AND tail-batch-size > 10 => page SRE. Owner: Benji. ETA: 2026-11-02 (add rule), 2026-11-04 (validate).

Longer-term initiatives (tracked separately):
- Adaptive prefetch window learning (ML-based suggestion) — prototype in Optimize backlog (topic for Jan sprint).
- Formalize kernel compatibility matrix so fallbacks only trigger when truly incompatible (research item).

Open questions / discussion notes:
- Why did the kernel fallback path drop KV coalescing? There is an implicit dependency on the per-request buffer layout; we need a short design doc explaining the invariants the coalescer relies on. Action: Diego to draft by 2026-11-06.
- Could we proactively warm KV cache on predicted spikes? Early simulation suggests warmup reduces p95 by ~35% for synthetic workload. Action: Claire to run 2 controlled warmup experiments on staging by 2026-11-11.
- Does the batching cap increase cause higher GPU memory pressure under certain seq-length distributions? Aisha to validate with memprof on dedicated ci pool by 2026-11-04.

Experiment logs and notes (informal):
- local/bench/exp-2026-10-25: toggled small-kernel inlining -> saw 18% CPU decrease on long-seq but 40% increase in kernel-fallbacks on mixed traffic. (Diego)
- stag/kv-warmup-1: prefetch priming for 60s before traffic surge -> hit-rate improved from 62% -> 82% in window; no spillover observed. (Claire)
- perf/regression-check-1347: PR 1347 fixed an unrelated GC issue but increased gating on kernel selection. Rolled back during incident. (Benji)

Action items (owner / due):
- Diego: implement batcher backoff change + draft kernel invariants doc (due 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-06).
- Aisha: apply autoscaler hysteresis change and run memprof baseline (due 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04).
- Benji: create the new alert and validate false-positive rate (due 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-04).
- Claire: run staged KV warmup experiments and summarize results for next sync (due 2026-11-11).
- Ellen: include incident timeline and customer impact note in the runbook (due 2026-11-05).

Meeting transcript highlights (selected):
- 00:07 Claire: "We need to stop the domino effect — cascade from prefetch miss into fallback is the biggest risk."
- 00:18 Diego: "Small-kernel path is beneficial mostly for long continuous sequences; we accidentally made it the default for certain batch shapes."
- 00:34 Benji: "Obs shows the prefetch window drop is the earliest signal — we should instrument that better in traces."

Retro takeaways:
- Incidents often arise from cross-layer timing assumptions (batcher <-> prefetch <-> kernel). Invest in small, focused invariants docs to avoid implicit coupling.
- Feature flags + canary gating for kernel changes need to include a prefetch-hit check to avoid full flip in mixed traffic.
- Observability: add a compact dashboard (1-page) that shows prefetch-hit, tail-batch-size, kernel-fallback-rate per pool. Benji to prototype.

Next sync: 2026-11-09, 10:30 PT. Agenda: review Diego's backoff PR, autoscaler hysteresis validation, warmup experiment results.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (scratchpad):
- Add links to the three incident traces (will paste after S3 replication): TRACE-3124, TRACE-3125, TRACE-3126.
- Remind infra to hold capacity for canary on 2026-11-05 deploy window.
- Follow up separately on customer communication draft (ops) — Ellen to own.

Attachments (work items):
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1347
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-3124
- Slack thread: https://squad-channel.slack.com/archives/C02SERVE123/p1698456000000

End of notes.
summary: Weekly serving-runtime retro focused on spillover incidents caused by interactions between batching, KV prefetch, and kernel fallback. Short-term mitigations and owners assigned; experiments planned.
